record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.context_brief: Regularity of eggs in even characteristic
record.original_question: If O(n, 2n, q) is an egg in even characteristic, is it always regular, in the sense of the paper’s notion of a regular pseudo-ovoid?

evidence.quote: 2. Is any egg O(n, 2n, q), q even, regular?
For n = m such a set O(n, m, q) is called a pseudo-ovoid or a generalized ovoid or an [n − 1]-ovoid or an egg of PG(2n + m − 1, q); a [0]-ovoid of PG(3, q) is just an ovoid of PG(3, q).
Here, we speak of a regular pseudo-oval, respectively a regular pseudo-ovoid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $n\ge 1$ be an integer. In the finite projective space $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$, an egg (also called a pseudo-ovoid, generalized ovoid, or $[n-1]$-ovoid), denoted $O(n,2n,q)$, is a family $\mathcal{E}$ of $q^{2n}+1$ pairwise disjoint $(n-1)$-dimensional subspaces such that:

(i) any three distinct elements of $\mathcal{E}$ span a $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace; and
(ii) at every element $E\in\mathcal{E}$ there exists a unique $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace $T_E$ (the tangent space at $E$) which contains $E$ and is disjoint from every other element of $\mathcal{E}$.

Such an egg is called regular (a regular pseudo-ovoid) if the $q^{2n}+1$ tangent spaces $\{T_E : E\in\mathcal{E}\}$ form the dual of an egg in $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$; equivalently, every hyperplane of $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$ either contains exactly one tangent space or contains exactly $q^n+1$ tangent spaces.

Question: Suppose $q$ is even. Is every egg $O(n,2n,q)$ in $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$ necessarily regular?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every egg O(n,2n,q) in even characteristic is regular is a well-known open problem in finite geometry. Recent partial results (e.g., classifications of eggs containing a pseudo-conic, characterizations of classical eggs, and progress on translation generalized ovals in even characteristic) address special cases but do not resolve the general question. No source found that fully settles it.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n−1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-pointed conic
status_evidence.snippet: The egg O(n,2n,q) of PG(4n−1,q), q even, is classical if and only if either O is good at some element and contains at least one pseudo-conic, or O contains at least two intersecting pseudo-conics.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works obtain only partial/conditional characterizations of eggs in even characteristic, suggesting the general regularity question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Translation Generalized Quadrangles In Even Characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: Translation generalized quadrangles in even characteristic — characterizations of classical TGQs under additional hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results in even characteristic require additional hypotheses, indicating the unconditional regularity of eggs in even characteristic is not yet established.
